title: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR of February 29 is February 28 of the year before
query: EVALUATE CALCULATETABLE ( VAR R = SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR ( 'Date'[Date] ) RETURN ROW ( "Min", MINX ( R, 'Date'[Date] ), "Max", MAXX ( R, 'Date'[Date] ), "Days", COUNTROWS ( R ), "Sales", CALCULATE ( [Sales], R ) ), 'Date'[Date] = DATE ( 2024, 2, 29 ) )

source.quote: Internally SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR corresponds to the following call of DATEADD :
The last day of the shifted month is returned if the day does not exist in the shifted month.
source.supports: a day that does not exist in the target month becomes its last day

derivation: February 2024 is not fully selected, so the day is shifted on its own. February 29, 2023 does not exist; the last day of the shifted month, February 28, 2023, is returned. Sales on that date: 40.
alternative: SQLBI states the "last day of the shifted month" rule in its sentence about the DAY interval. If a date with no counterpart is dropped instead, the result is an empty table: [Min] and [Max] BLANK, [Days] BLANK, [Sales] BLANK.
